title: 2009 AMC 12B Problem 13
statement: Triangle \(ABC\) has \(AB = 13\) and \(AC = 15,\) and the altitude to \(BC\) has length \(12.\) What is the sum of the two possible values of \(BC?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(D\) be the foot of the altitude from \(A.\) Then \(BD = \sqrt{13^2 - 12^2} = 5\) and \(DC = \sqrt{15^2 - 12^2} = 9.\)

If \(D\) lies between \(B\) and \(C,\) then \(BC = 5 + 9 = 14\); if the triangle is obtuse, \(BC = 9 - 5 = 4.\) The sum is \(14 + 4 = 18.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: The foot of the altitude splits \(BC\); use the Pythagorean theorem in the two right triangles
The foot distances are \(\sqrt{13^2 - 12^2} = 5\) and \(\sqrt{15^2 - 12^2} = 9\); \(BC\) is their sum or difference
